```{r data loading and cleaning, cache=TRUE}
# read in data and clean 

data <- read_excel("/data/survey_for_analysis_100125.xlsx")

data <- data %>%
    mutate(
    jewish = case_when(
      religmod == "Jewish" ~ 1,
      
      # atheist, agnostic, nothing in particular, or NA but ID as Jewish
      (religmod %in% c("Atheist", "Agnostic", "Nothing in particular") | is.na(religmod)) &
        relconsider_1 == "Yes, consider myself this" ~ 1,
      
      # "something else" but also ID as jewish and doesn't identify as another religion in text
      religmod == "Something else (please specify)" &
        relconsider_1 == "Yes, consider myself this" &
        (is.na(religmod_11_text) |
           religmod_11_text %in% c(
             "Secular Jew",
             "Atheist-Humanist",
             "Non religious Jew",
             "secular jewish",
             "Humanist",
             "Secular Humanist",
             "Jewish socially, agnostic religiously",
             "secular Jewish",
             "You’re affiliation w Harvard makes you anti-semetic",
             "Human Being",
             "Secular",
             "spiritual Jew",
             "Non practicing Jew",
             "Earth based practices but raised Jewish",
             "Culturally Jewish, but agnostic",
             "Spiritual",
             "Raised Jewish, not observant",
             "Former Jew"
           )
        ) ~ 1,
      
      TRUE ~ 0
    )
  )

# read in pew data
pew <- read_dta("/data/pew2020/Jewish Americans in 2020 Extended Dataset.dta")

# make pew data survey design
pew <- pew %>%
  # filter out for self ID jew by religion or culture/ethnicity
  filter(JEWISHCAT < 3) %>%  mutate(across(c(SEXASK, AGE4CAT, PARTY, REGION), ~ as_factor(.x, levels = "default"))) %>%
  # make into factor
  mutate(across(
    c(BRANCH, ATTEND1, JEWIMP, MEMSYN1, KOSHER, SEDER,
      OWNOB_A, OWNOB_B, OWNOB_C, OWNOB_D, MITZVAH, BELONG, JFRIEND),
    ~ as_factor(.x, levels = "default") 
  ))

# define pew survey design
pew.svy <- svydesign(ids = ~1, data = pew, weights = ~EXTWEIGHT)


# create unique rowid
data$caseid <- 1:nrow(data)

# create birthdecade column
data <- data %>%
  mutate(birthdecade = if_else(
    !is.na(birthyear),
    paste0(str_sub(birthyear, 1, 3), "0s"),
    NA_character_
  )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    birth_year = as.numeric(substr(birthdate, nchar(birthdate) - 3, nchar(birthdate))),
    age = 2025 - birth_year
  ) %>%
  mutate(
  responded = if_else(`_merge` == "Matched (3)", 1, 0)
) %>%
  mutate(sampled = if_else(`_merge` == "Master only (1)", 0, 1))

```

```{r weights, include=FALSE}
# post-stratify to our sample ---------------------------------------------

# identify the population (all rows) and survey sample (Matched (3))
pop <- data
sample <- pop %>% filter(`_merge` == "Matched (3)") %>% filter(jewish ==1 )

# calculate population marginal probabilities
pop_margins <- list(
  state = prop.table(table(pop$state)),
  gender = prop.table(table(pop$gender)),
  party = prop.table(table(pop$party)),
  birthdecade = prop.table(table(pop$birthdecade))
)

# turn sample into factors
sample <- sample %>%
  mutate(
    state = factor(state, levels = names(pop_margins$state)),
    gender = factor(gender, levels = names(pop_margins$gender)),
    party = factor(party, levels = names(pop_margins$party)),
    birthdecade = factor(birthdecade, levels = names(pop_margins$birthdecade))
  )

# create named list of sample variables
sample_vars <- list(
  state = sample$state,
  gender = sample$gender,
  party = sample$party,
  birthdecade = sample$birthdecade
)

# get weights -- have to turn sample into data.frame because it hates tibbles
rake_result <- anesrake(
  pop_margins,
  as.data.frame(sample),
  caseid = sample$caseid,
)

# add raked weights to sample df
sample$weight_raked <- rake_result$weightvec

rm(pop, pop_margins, rake_result, sample_vars)



# pew weights -------------------------------------------------------------

# get marginal probabilities

pew_margins <- list(
  gender.pew = prop.table(svytable(~SEXASK, design = pew.svy)),
  age.pew = prop.table(svytable(~AGE4CAT, design = pew.svy)),
  party.pew = prop.table(svytable(~PARTY, design = pew.svy)),
  region = prop.table(svytable(~REGION, design = pew.svy))
)

# set classifications for states into census regions
northeast <- c("CT", "ME", "MA", "NH", "RI", "VT", "NJ", "NY", "PA")
midwest   <- c("IL", "IN", "MI", "OH", "WI", "IA", "KS", "MN", "MO", "NE", "ND", "SD")
south     <- c("DE", "FL", "GA", "MD", "NC", "SC", "VA", "DC", "WV",
               "AL", "KY", "MS", "TN", "AR", "LA", "OK", "TX")
west      <- c("AZ", "CO", "ID", "MT", "NV", "NM", "UT", "WY",
               "AK", "CA", "HI", "OR", "WA")

# add new columns to match with pew
sample <- sample %>%
  mutate(
    gender.pew = recode(gender,
                        "M" = "1 = MALE",
                        "F" = "2 = FEMALE",
                        .default = "99 = NOT ANSWERED"
    ),
    
    age.pew = case_when(
      !is.na(birthyear) & birthyear >= 1996 ~ "18-29",
      birthyear >= 1974 & birthyear <= 1995 ~ "30-49",
      birthyear >= 1960 & birthyear <= 1973 ~ "50-64",
      birthyear < 1960 ~ "65+",
      TRUE ~ "NO ANSWER"
    ),
    
    party.pew = recode(party,
                       "Republican" = "1 = REPUBLICAN",
                       "Democratic" = "2 = DEMOCRAT",
                       "Registered Independent" = "3 = INDEPENDENT",
                       "Non-Partisan" = "3 = INDEPENDENT",
                       "Libertarian" = "4 = SOMETHING ELSE",
                       "Constitution" = "4 = SOMETHING ELSE",
                       "Independence" = "4 = SOMETHING ELSE",
                       "American Independent" = "4 = SOMETHING ELSE",
                       "Other" = "4 = SOMETHING ELSE",
                       "Unknown" = "99 = NOT ANSWERED",
                       .default = "99 = NOT ANSWERED"
    ),
    
    region = case_when(
      state %in% northeast ~ "NORTHEAST",
      state %in% midwest ~ "MIDWEST",
      state %in% south ~ "SOUTH",
      state %in% west ~ "WEST",
      TRUE ~ "99 = NOT ANSWERED"
    )) %>%
  mutate(
    gender.pew = factor(gender.pew, levels = names(pew_margins$gender.pew)),
    age.pew    = factor(age.pew,    levels = names(pew_margins$age)),
    party.pew  = factor(party.pew,  levels = names(pew_margins$party.pew)),
    region = factor(region, levels = names(pew_margins$region))
  )

# rake to pew
rake_result <- anesrake(
  pew_margins,
  dataframe = as.data.frame(sample),
  caseid = sample$caseid
)

sample$weight_pew_raked <- rake_result$weightvec


rm(pew_margins, rake_result, midwest, northeast, south, west)

```


```{r ipw-weights}
# IPW weight --------------------------------------------------------------

# get IPW weights
sample <- sample %>%
  mutate(weight_ipw = 1/sampling_prob)

# trim in different levels for sensitivity testing
sample <- sample %>%
  mutate(weight_ipw_10 = case_when(
    weight_ipw > quantile(sample$weight_ipw, probs = 0.90) ~ quantile(sample$weight_ipw, probs = 0.90),
    weight_ipw < quantile(sample$weight_ipw, probs = 0.10) ~ quantile(sample$weight_ipw, probs = 0.10),
    TRUE ~ weight_ipw
  )) %>%
  mutate(weight_ipw_8 = case_when(
    weight_ipw > quantile(sample$weight_ipw, probs = 0.92) ~ quantile(sample$weight_ipw, probs = 0.92),
    weight_ipw < quantile(sample$weight_ipw, probs = 0.08) ~ quantile(sample$weight_ipw, probs = 0.08),
    TRUE ~ weight_ipw
  )) %>%
  mutate(weight_ipw_12 = case_when(
    weight_ipw > quantile(sample$weight_ipw, probs = 0.88) ~ quantile(sample$weight_ipw, probs = 0.88),
    weight_ipw < quantile(sample$weight_ipw, probs = 0.12) ~ quantile(sample$weight_ipw, probs = 0.12),
    TRUE ~ weight_ipw
  )) %>%
  mutate(weight_ipw_5 = case_when(
    weight_ipw > quantile(sample$weight_ipw, probs = 0.95) ~ quantile(sample$weight_ipw, probs = 0.95),
    weight_ipw < quantile(sample$weight_ipw, probs = 0.05) ~ quantile(sample$weight_ipw, probs = 0.05),
    TRUE ~ weight_ipw
  ))

```

```{r ipw plus raking, include=FALSE, cache=TRUE}
# estimated margins weights -----------------------------------------------

margins <- read_csv(
  "estimated_weights_overall_drop_missing.csv"
)

# combine ages into four categories
age_margins <- margins %>%
  filter(X_variable == "Age") %>%
  mutate(
    age = as.numeric(Variable_Level),
    age.margins = case_when(
      age >= 18 & age <= 29 ~ "18-29",
      age >= 30 & age <= 49 ~ "30-49",
      age >= 50 & age <= 64 ~ "50-64",
      age >= 65 ~ "65+"
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(age.margins) %>%
  summarise(estimate = sum(estimate), .groups = "drop")

# combine small party categories
party_margins <- margins %>%
  filter(X_variable == "Party") %>%
  mutate(
    party.margins = case_when(
      Variable_Level == "Democratic" ~ "Democratic",
      Variable_Level == "Republican" ~ "Republican",
      Variable_Level %in% c("Registered Independent", "Non-Partisan") ~
        "Independent",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(party.margins) %>%
  summarise(estimate = sum(estimate), .groups = "drop")

gender_margins <- margins %>%
  filter(X_variable == "Gender")

# get marginal probabilities
estimated_margins <- list(
  gender.margins = setNames(
    gender_margins$estimate,
    gender_margins$Variable_Level
  ),
  age.margins = setNames(
    age_margins$estimate,
    age_margins$age.margins
  ),
  party.margins = setNames(
    party_margins$estimate,
    party_margins$party.margins
  )
)

# ensure each set of probabilities sums to 1
estimated_margins <- lapply(
  estimated_margins,
  function(x) x / sum(x)
)

# add new columns to match the margins
sample <- sample %>%
  mutate(
    gender.margins = as.character(gender),

    age.margins = case_when(
      age >= 18 & age <= 29 ~ "18-29",
      age >= 30 & age <= 49 ~ "30-49",
      age >= 50 & age <= 64 ~ "50-64",
      age >= 65 ~ "65+"
    ),

    party.margins = case_when(
      party == "Democratic" ~ "Democratic",
      party == "Republican" ~ "Republican",
      party %in% c("Registered Independent", "Non-Partisan") ~
        "Independent",
      is.na(party) ~ NA_character_,
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    gender.margins = factor(
      gender.margins,
      levels = names(estimated_margins$gender.margins)
    ),
    age.margins = factor(
      age.margins,
      levels = names(estimated_margins$age.margins)
    ),
    party.margins = factor(
      party.margins,
      levels = names(estimated_margins$party.margins)
    )
  )

# AJPP regional margins ---------------------------------------------------

p_state_gvn_R1 <- readRDS("p_state_gvn_R1.RDS")

# set classifications for states into census regions
northeast <- c("CT", "ME", "MA", "NH", "RI", "VT", "NJ", "NY", "PA")
midwest   <- c("IL", "IN", "MI", "OH", "WI", "IA", "KS", "MN", "MO", "NE", "ND", "SD")
south     <- c("DE", "FL", "GA", "MD", "NC", "SC", "VA", "DC", "WV",
               "AL", "KY", "MS", "TN", "AR", "LA", "OK", "TX")
west      <- c("AZ", "CO", "ID", "MT", "NV", "NM", "UT", "WY",
               "AK", "CA", "HI", "OR", "WA")

# aggregate state proportions to regions
region_margins <- c(
  "NORTHEAST" = sum(p_state_gvn_R1[northeast]),
  "MIDWEST" = sum(p_state_gvn_R1[midwest]),
  "SOUTH" = sum(p_state_gvn_R1[south]),
  "WEST" = sum(p_state_gvn_R1[west])
)

# add region to the existing age, gender, and party targets
estimated_margins$region.margins <- region_margins / sum(region_margins)

# create matching respondent categories
sample <- sample %>%
  mutate(
    region.margins = case_when(
      state %in% northeast ~ "NORTHEAST",
      state %in% midwest ~ "MIDWEST",
      state %in% south ~ "SOUTH",
      state %in% west ~ "WEST",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    region.margins = factor(
      region.margins,
      levels = names(estimated_margins$region.margins)
    )
  )

# rake to estimated margins using trimmed IPW
rake_result <- anesrake(
  estimated_margins,
  dataframe = as.data.frame(sample),
  caseid = sample$caseid,
  weightvec = sample$weight_ipw_10
)

# add raked weights to sample
sample$weight_ipw_raked_margins <- rake_result$weightvec

rm(margins, age_margins, party_margins, gender_margins,
   estimated_margins, rake_result)
```

```{r svydesigns}
# define svydesigns -------------------------------------------------------

# define survey design for post-stratify weights
svy.raked <- svydesign(ids = ~1, data = sample, weights = ~weight_raked)

# define unweighted survey design
svy.unweighted <- svydesign(ids = ~1, data = sample, weights = ~1)

# define pew raked survey design
svy.raked.pew <- svydesign(ids = ~1, data = sample, weights = ~weight_pew_raked)

# define ipw survey designs
svy.ipw <- svydesign(ids = ~1, data = sample, weights = ~weight_ipw)

svy.ipw.5 <- svydesign(ids = ~1, data = sample, weights = ~weight_ipw_5)

svy.ipw.8 <- svydesign(ids = ~1, data = sample, weights = ~weight_ipw_8)

svy.ipw.10 <- svydesign(ids = ~1, data = sample, weights = ~weight_ipw_10)

svy.ipw.12 <- svydesign(ids = ~1, data = sample, weights = ~weight_ipw_12)

svy.ipw.raked.sample <- svydesign(ids = ~1, data = sample, weights = ~weight_ipw_raked_sample)

svy.ipw.raked.pew <- svydesign(ids = ~1, data = sample, weights = ~weight_ipw_raked_pew)

svy.ipw.raked.margins <- svydesign(
  ids = ~1,
  data = sample,
  weights = ~weight_ipw_raked_margins
)
```

```{r  functions}
get_results <- function(design, var, source_label) {
  props <- svymean(as.formula(paste0("~", var)), design = design, na.rm = TRUE)
  data.frame(
    Estimate = coef(props),
    SE = SE(props),
    confint(props)
  ) %>%
    rename_with(~ c("CI_lower", "CI_upper"), .cols = c("X2.5..", "X97.5..")) %>%
    rownames_to_column("Variable") %>%
    mutate(
      Variable = toupper(Variable),
      Source   = source_label
    )
}



# survey designs list 

designs <- list(
  pew          = pew.svy,
  unweighted   = svy.unweighted,
  raked.sample = svy.raked,  
  raked.pew    = svy.raked.pew,
  ipw          = svy.ipw,
  ipw.5        = svy.ipw.5,
  ipw.8        = svy.ipw.8,
  ipw.10       = svy.ipw.10,
  ipw.12       = svy.ipw.12,
  ipw.raked.sample = svy.ipw.raked.sample,
  ipw.raked.pew = svy.ipw.raked.pew,
  ipw.raked.margins = svy.ipw.raked.margins
)


# defines the variable names
var_map_for <- function(sample_var, pew_var) {
  vm <- setNames(rep(sample_var, length(designs)), names(designs))
  vm[["pew"]] <- pew_var
  vm
}

```



# Main charts and analysis

## Branch


```{r main-branch, fig.height=3, fig.width=7}
# define variables
var_map <- var_map_for(sample_var = "branch", pew_var = "BRANCH")

# run for each design with correct variable
branch_long <- imap_dfr(
  designs,
  ~ get_results(.x, var_map[[.y]], .y)
) %>%
  filter(Source %in% c(
    "pew", "ipw.raked.pew", "ipw.raked.margins", "ipw.10"
  )) %>%
  mutate(
    Variable = recode(
      Variable,
      "BRANCHREFORM"       = "Reform",
      "BRANCHCONSERVATIVE" = "Conservative",
      "BRANCHORTHODOX"     = "Orthodox"
    ),
    Variable = if_else(
      Variable %in% c("Conservative", "Orthodox", "Reform"),
      Variable,
      "Something Else / None"
    ),
    Source = factor(
      Source,
      levels = c(
        "pew", "ipw.raked.pew", "ipw.raked.margins", "ipw.10"
      )
    ),
    Variable = factor(
      Variable,
      levels = c(
        "Reform", "Conservative", "Orthodox",
        "Something Else / None"
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(Source, Variable) %>%
  summarise(
    across(where(is.numeric), sum, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# plot results
library(ggplot2)

dodge_width <- 0.5

# compute significance vs. Pew
branch_sig <- branch_long %>%
  group_by(Variable) %>%
  mutate(
    pew_est = Estimate[Source == "pew"],
    pew_se  = SE[Source == "pew"],
    z       = abs((Estimate - pew_est) / sqrt(SE^2 + pew_se^2)),
    pval    = 2 * (1 - pnorm(z)),
    sig     = pval < 0.05
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# source order
legend_order <- rev(c(
  "pew",
  "ipw.raked.pew",
  "ipw.raked.margins",
  "ipw.10"
))

# offsets for significance stars
offsets <- c(
  "ipw.10" = -1.5,
  "ipw.raked.margins" = -0.5,
  "ipw.raked.pew" = 0.5,
  "pew" = 1.5
)

branch_sig <- branch_sig %>%
  mutate(
    Variable = forcats::fct_rev(Variable),
    Source = factor(Source, levels = legend_order),
    x_pos = as.numeric(Variable) +
      offsets[as.character(Source)] * dodge_width / 4
  )

# plot
ggplot(
  branch_sig,
  aes(
    x = Variable,
    y = Estimate * 100,
    color = Source,
    group = Source
  )
) +
  geom_point(
    position = position_dodge(width = dodge_width)
  ) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      ymin = CI_lower * 100,
      ymax = CI_upper * 100
    ),
    width = 0.2,
    position = position_dodge(width = dodge_width)) +
  # ) +
  # geom_text(
```

```{r main-other-trimmed, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
# func to compute and label significance vs Pew
compute_sig_vs_pew <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    group_by(VariableClean, Question) %>%
    mutate(
      pew_est = Estimate[Source == "pew"],
      pew_se  = SE[Source == "pew"],
      z       = abs((Estimate - pew_est) / sqrt(SE^2 + pew_se^2)),
      pval    = 2 * (1 - pnorm(z)),
      sig     = if_else(pval < 0.05, TRUE, FALSE)
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
}

# func to fuzzy-match Pew categories and unify variable labels
unify_labels <- function(df, var_prefix, question_label) {
  raked <- df %>% filter(Source == "raked.sample") %>% select(Variable)
  pew   <- df %>% filter(Source == "pew") %>% select(Variable)
  
  match <- stringdist_inner_join(
    raked, pew, by = "Variable", method = "jw", max_dist = 0.3, distance_col = "dist"
  ) %>%
    group_by(Variable.x) %>%
    slice_min(dist, n = 1) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    transmute(Var_raked = Variable.x, Var_pew = Variable.y)
  
  df %>%
    left_join(match, by = c("Variable" = "Var_pew")) %>%
    mutate(
      VariableUnified = coalesce(Var_raked, Variable),
      VariableClean = str_to_title(
        str_trim(str_remove(VariableUnified, paste0("^(?:", var_prefix, "|[0-9]+\\s*=\\s*)")))
      ),
      Question = question_label
    ) %>%
    select(-Var_raked, -VariableUnified)
}
```

```{r main-updated-summary-statistics}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(survey)

# add the original nine-item count to a design
add_behavior_count <- function(design, pew = FALSE) {

  if (pew) {
    item_variables <- c(
      "ATTEND1", "MEMSYN1", "KOSHER", "SEDER",
      "OWNOB_C", "OWNOB_D", "OWNOB_A", "OWNOB_B", "MITZVAH"
    )

    yes_values <- c(
      "1 = MORE THAN ONCE A WEEK",
      "1 = YES",
      "1 = YES, I KEEP KOSHER AND I SEPARATE MEAT AND DAIRY",
      "1 = YES, HELD OR ATTENDED A SEDER",
      "1 = YES, OWN THIS",
      "1 = YES, OWN THIS",
      "1 = YES, OWN THIS",
      "1 = YES, OWN THIS",
      "1 = YES"
    )
  } else {
    item_variables <- c(
      "attend1", "memsyn1", "kosher", "seder",
      "ownob_3", "ownob_4", "ownob_1", "ownob_2", "mitzvah"
    )

    yes_values <- c(
      "More than once a week",
      "Yes",
      "Yes, I keep kosher and I separate meat and dairy",
      "Yes, held or attended a Seder",
      "Yes, own this",
      "Yes, own this",
      "Yes, own this",
      "Yes, own this",
      "Yes"
    )
  }

  indicators <- map2(
    item_variables,
    yes_values,
    ~as.numeric(design$variables[[.x]] == .y)
  )

  # deal with missing items
  design$variables$beh_count_9 <- Reduce(`+`, indicators)

  design
}

# prepare pew comparison design
pew_summary_design <- subset(
  pew.svy,
  JEWISHCAT %in% c(1, 2)
)

pew_summary_design <- update(
  pew_summary_design,
  cultural_ethnic = as.numeric(JEWISHCAT == 2)
)

pew_summary_design <- add_behavior_count(
  pew_summary_design,
  pew = TRUE
)

# prepare BISG comparison designs
prepare_summary_design <- function(design) {
  design <- subset(design, jewish == 1)

  design <- update(
    design,
    cultural_ethnic = as.numeric(religmod != "Jewish")
  )

  add_behavior_count(design, pew = FALSE)
}

summary_designs <- list(
  "2020 Pew Survey" = pew_summary_design,
  "IPW raked to estimated margins" =
    prepare_summary_design(svy.ipw.raked.margins),
  "IPW raked to Pew" =
    prepare_summary_design(svy.ipw.raked.pew)
)

# calculate estimates, standard errors, and confidence intervals
get_summary_stats <- function(design, estimator) {

  cultural_mean <- svymean(
    ~cultural_ethnic,
    design = design,
    na.rm = TRUE
  )

  cultural_prop <- svyciprop(
    ~cultural_ethnic,
    design = design,
    method = "logit",
    level = 0.95,
    na.rm = TRUE
  )

  cultural_ci <- confint(cultural_prop)

  activities_mean <- svymean(
    ~beh_count_9,
    design = design,
    na.rm = TRUE
  )

  activities_ci <- confint(activities_mean, level = 0.95)

  tibble(
    Estimator = estimator,
    Statistic = c(
      "Cultural/ethnic but not Jewish by religion (%)",
      "Mean number of activities (0–9)"
    ),
    Estimate = c(
      as.numeric(coef(cultural_mean)) * 100,
      as.numeric(coef(activities_mean))
    ),
    SE = c(
      as.numeric(SE(cultural_mean)) * 100,
      as.numeric(SE(activities_mean))
    ),
    CI_lower = c(
      as.numeric(cultural_ci[1]) * 100,
      as.numeric(activities_ci[1])
    ),
    CI_upper = c(
      as.numeric(cultural_ci[2]) * 100,
      as.numeric(activities_ci[2])
    ),
    N = c(
      sum(!is.na(design$variables$cultural_ethnic)),
      sum(!is.na(design$variables$beh_count_9))
    )
  )
}

summary_estimates <- imap_dfr(
  summary_designs,
  ~get_summary_stats(.x, .y)
)

# pew estimates and standard errors for the comparisons
pew_reference <- summary_estimates %>%
  filter(Estimator == "2020 Pew Survey") %>%
  select(
    Statistic,
    Pew_estimate = Estimate,
    Pew_SE = SE
  )

# wald tests against pew
updated_summary_stats <- summary_estimates %>%
  left_join(pew_reference, by = "Statistic") %>%
  mutate(
    Difference_vs_Pew = if_else(
      Estimator == "2020 Pew Survey",
      NA_real_,
      Estimate - Pew_estimate
    ),
    Difference_SE = sqrt(SE^2 + Pew_SE^2),
    z = Difference_vs_Pew / Difference_SE,
    p_value_vs_Pew = 2 * pnorm(abs(z), lower.tail = FALSE)
  ) %>%
  select(
    Estimator,
    Statistic,
    Estimate,
    CI_lower,
    CI_upper,
    N,
    Difference_vs_Pew,
    p_value_vs_Pew
  )

updated_summary_stats %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)

```

```{r main-practice-significance-estimated-margins}
library(purrr)
library(survey)

# get jewish respondents under the estimated-margin weights
practice_design <- subset(
  svy.ipw.raked.margins,
  jewish == 1
)

# same nine measures and response definitions 
practice_items <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Measure, ~sample_var, ~pew_var, ~sample_yes, ~pew_yes,
  "Attend more than once a week",
  "attend1", "ATTEND1",
  "More than once a week", "1 = MORE THAN ONCE A WEEK",

  "Keep Kosher - Strictly",
  "kosher", "KOSHER",
  "Yes, I keep kosher and I separate meat and dairy",
  "1 = YES, I KEEP KOSHER AND I SEPARATE MEAT AND DAIRY",

  "Synagogue Members",
  "memsyn1", "MEMSYN1",
  "Yes", "1 = YES",

  "Had Bar/Bat Mitzvah",
  "mitzvah", "MITZVAH",
  "Yes", "1 = YES",

  "Held/Attended Seder",
  "seder", "SEDER",
  "Yes, held or attended a Seder",
  "1 = YES, HELD OR ATTENDED A SEDER",

  "Own Seder plate",
  "ownob_3", "OWNOB_C",
  "Yes, own this", "1 = YES, OWN THIS",

  "Own Siddur",
  "ownob_4", "OWNOB_D",
  "Yes, own this", "1 = YES, OWN THIS",

  "Own Menorah",
  "ownob_1", "OWNOB_A",
  "Yes, own this", "1 = YES, OWN THIS",

  "Own Mezuzah",
  "ownob_2", "OWNOB_B",
  "Yes, own this", "1 = YES, OWN THIS"
)

# estimate each binary measure using its survey weights
get_practice_estimate <- function(design, variable, yes_value) {
  design$variables$practice_indicator <- as.numeric(
    as.character(design$variables[[variable]]) == yes_value
  )

  estimate <- svymean(
    ~practice_indicator,
    design = design,
    na.rm = TRUE
  )

  c(
    estimate = as.numeric(coef(estimate)),
    se = as.numeric(SE(estimate))
  )
}

# wald tests against pew
practice_tests <- pmap_dfr(
  practice_items,
  function(Measure, sample_var, pew_var, sample_yes, pew_yes) {

    bisg_result <- get_practice_estimate(
      practice_design, sample_var, sample_yes
    )

    pew_result <- get_practice_estimate(
      pew.svy, pew_var, pew_yes
    )

    difference <- bisg_result[["estimate"]] -
      pew_result[["estimate"]]

    difference_se <- sqrt(
      bisg_result[["se"]]^2 + pew_result[["se"]]^2
    )

    z <- difference / difference_se
    p_value <- 2 * pnorm(abs(z), lower.tail = FALSE)

    tibble(
      Measure = Measure,
      Pew_percent = pew_result[["estimate"]] * 100,
      BISG_percent = bisg_result[["estimate"]] * 100,
      Difference_percentage_points = difference * 100,
      p_value = p_value,
      Significant_at_5_percent = p_value < 0.05
    )
  }
)

practice_tests %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 4)

# list significant results
significant_measures <- practice_tests %>%
  filter(Significant_at_5_percent) %>%
  pull(Measure)

if (length(significant_measures) == 0) {
  cat("\nNo measures differ significantly from Pew at the 5% level.")
} else {
  cat(
    "\nMeasures differing significantly from Pew at the 5% level:\n",
    paste(significant_measures, collapse = "\n")
  )
}
```

```{r main-practice-significance-all-weights}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(survey)

# three weighting designs
practice_designs <- list(
  "IPW with 10/90 trimming only" = svy.ipw.10,
  "IPW raked to estimated margins" = svy.ipw.raked.margins,
  "IPW raked to Pew" = svy.ipw.raked.pew
)

# same nine measures and response definitions as the original figure
practice_items <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Measure, ~sample_var, ~pew_var, ~sample_yes, ~pew_yes,
  "Attend more than once a week",
  "attend1", "ATTEND1",
  "More than once a week", "1 = MORE THAN ONCE A WEEK",

  "Keep Kosher - Strictly",
  "kosher", "KOSHER",
  "Yes, I keep kosher and I separate meat and dairy",
  "1 = YES, I KEEP KOSHER AND I SEPARATE MEAT AND DAIRY",

  "Synagogue Members",
  "memsyn1", "MEMSYN1",
  "Yes", "1 = YES",

  "Had Bar/Bat Mitzvah",
  "mitzvah", "MITZVAH",
  "Yes", "1 = YES",

  "Held/Attended Seder",
  "seder", "SEDER",
  "Yes, held or attended a Seder",
  "1 = YES, HELD OR ATTENDED A SEDER",

  "Own Seder plate",
  "ownob_3", "OWNOB_C",
  "Yes, own this", "1 = YES, OWN THIS",

  "Own Siddur",
  "ownob_4", "OWNOB_D",
  "Yes, own this", "1 = YES, OWN THIS",

  "Own Menorah",
  "ownob_1", "OWNOB_A",
  "Yes, own this", "1 = YES, OWN THIS",

  "Own Mezuzah",
  "ownob_2", "OWNOB_B",
  "Yes, own this", "1 = YES, OWN THIS"
)

# estimate each binary measure using its survey weights
get_practice_estimate <- function(design, variable, yes_value) {
  design$variables$practice_indicator <- as.numeric(
    as.character(design$variables[[variable]]) == yes_value
  )

  estimate <- svymean(
    ~practice_indicator,
    design = design,
    na.rm = TRUE
  )

  c(
    estimate = as.numeric(coef(estimate)),
    se = as.numeric(SE(estimate))
  )
}

# compare each weighting design with pew
practice_tests <- imap_dfr(
  practice_designs,
  function(design, estimator) {

    # Jewish respondents only
    design <- subset(design, jewish == 1)

    pmap_dfr(
      practice_items,
      function(Measure, sample_var, pew_var, sample_yes, pew_yes) {

        bisg_result <- get_practice_estimate(
          design, sample_var, sample_yes
        )

        pew_result <- get_practice_estimate(
          pew.svy, pew_var, pew_yes
        )

        difference <- bisg_result[["estimate"]] -
          pew_result[["estimate"]]

        difference_se <- sqrt(
          bisg_result[["se"]]^2 + pew_result[["se"]]^2
        )

        z <- difference / difference_se
        p_value <- 2 * pnorm(abs(z), lower.tail = FALSE)

        tibble(
          Estimator = estimator,
          Measure = Measure,
          Pew_percent = pew_result[["estimate"]] * 100,
          BISG_percent = bisg_result[["estimate"]] * 100,
          Difference_percentage_points = difference * 100,
          p_value = p_value,
          Significant_at_5_percent = p_value < 0.05
        )
      }
    )
  }
)

# full results
practice_tests %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 4)

# find significant measures under each weighting design
practice_significance_summary <- practice_tests %>%
  group_by(Estimator) %>%
  summarise(
    Number_significant = sum(Significant_at_5_percent),
    Significant_measures = if (
      any(Significant_at_5_percent)
    ) {
      paste(
        Measure[Significant_at_5_percent],
        collapse = "; "
      )
    } else {
      "None"
    },
    .groups = "drop"
  )

practice_significance_summary %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

## Branch

```{r appendix-branch-app, fig.width=12, fig.height=6}
# weighting methods displayed in the appendix plots
# the shared setup above also creates two additional designs
designs <- designs[c(
  "pew", "unweighted", "raked.pew", "ipw", "ipw.5", "ipw.8",
  "ipw.10", "ipw.12", "ipw.raked.pew", "ipw.raked.margins"
)]

# same four denomination categories across all designs
branch_levels <- c(
  "Reform",
  "Conservative",
  "Orthodox",
  "Something Else / None"
)

# recode before estimation so the combined category has a correct SE and CI
branch_long <- imap_dfr(designs, function(design, source) {

  variable <- if (source == "pew") "BRANCH" else "branch"

  branch_text <- toupper(
    trimws(as.character(design$variables[[variable]]))
  )

  design$variables$branch_plot <- factor(
    case_when(
      is.na(branch_text) ~ NA_character_,
      branch_text == "REFORM" ~ "Reform",
      branch_text == "CONSERVATIVE" ~ "Conservative",
      branch_text == "ORTHODOX" ~ "Orthodox",
      TRUE ~ "Something Else / None"
    ),
    levels = branch_levels
  )

  get_results(design, "branch_plot", source)
}) %>%
  mutate(
    Variable = recode(
      Variable,
      "BRANCH_PLOTREFORM" = "Reform",
      "BRANCH_PLOTCONSERVATIVE" = "Conservative",
      "BRANCH_PLOTORTHODOX" = "Orthodox",
      "BRANCH_PLOTSOMETHING ELSE / NONE" = "Something Else / None"
    ),
    Source = factor(
      Source,
      levels = c(
        "pew", "unweighted", "raked.pew",
        "ipw", "ipw.5", "ipw.8", "ipw.10", "ipw.12",
        "ipw.raked.pew", "ipw.raked.margins"
      )
    ),
    Variable = factor(
      Variable,
      levels = branch_levels
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(Variable = forcats::fct_rev(Variable)) %>%
  mutate(Source = forcats::fct_rev(Source))

legend_order <- rev(c(
  "pew",
  "unweighted",
  "raked.pew",
  "ipw",
  "ipw.5",
  "ipw.8",
  "ipw.10",
  "ipw.12",
  "ipw.raked.pew",
  "ipw.raked.margins"
))

# plot results
ggplot(branch_long, aes(x = Variable, y = Estimate, color = Source)) +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = CI_lower, ymax = CI_upper),
    width = 0.2,
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)
  ) +
  xlab("") +
  scale_color_discrete(
    name = "Source",
    limits = legend_order,
    labels = c(
      "pew" = "2020 Pew Survey",
      "unweighted" = "2025 BISG Survey - Unweighted",
      "raked.pew" = "2025 BISG Survey - Raked to Pew",
      "ipw" = "2025 BISG Survey - IPW",
      "ipw.5" = "2025 BISG Survey - IPW (5/95 trim)",
      "ipw.8" = "2025 BISG Survey - IPW (8/92 trim)",
      "ipw.10" = "2025 BISG Survey - IPW (10/90 trim)",
      "ipw.12" = "2025 BISG Survey - IPW (12/88 trim)",
      "ipw.raked.pew" = "2025 BISG Survey - Raked to Pew post IPW",
      "ipw.raked.margins" =
        "2025 BISG Survey - Raked to Estimated Margins after IPW"
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey85", linewidth = 0.5),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
    plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5)
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = seq(1.5, 3.5, by = 1),
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 0.3,
    alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  guides(color = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE))
```

## Synagogue Attendance

```{r appendix-attend plot, fig.height=8, fig.width=12, echo=FALSE}
# get variables
var_map <- var_map_for(sample_var = "attend1", pew_var = "ATTEND1")


# compute results for all designs
att_all <- imap_dfr(designs, ~ get_results(.x, var_map[[.y]], .y))

# fuzzy match pew to one of the other samples -- select pew and one other
att_raked <- att_all %>% filter(Source == "unweighted") %>% select(Variable, Estimate:CI_upper)
att_pew   <- att_all %>% filter(Source == "pew") %>% select(Variable, Estimate:CI_upper)

# fuzzy match
att_match <- stringdist_inner_join(
  att_raked, att_pew, by = "Variable",
  method = "jw", max_dist = 0.3, distance_col = "dist"
) %>%
  group_by(Variable.x) %>%
  slice_min(dist, n = 1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  transmute(Var_raked = Variable.x, Var_pew = Variable.y)

# apply our labels to pew and join together
att_all_unified <- att_all %>%
  left_join(att_match, by = c("Variable" = "Var_pew")) %>%
  # if there is a var_raked match, use that; if not, use original
  mutate(VariableUnified = coalesce(Var_raked, Variable)) %>%
  select(-Var_raked)

# clean variable text 
att_all_unified <- att_all_unified %>%
  mutate(VariableClean = str_to_title(str_trim(str_remove(VariableUnified, "^(ATTEND1|ATTEND)"))))

# define the levels we want
att_levels <- c(
  "More Than Once A Week", "Once A Week", "Once Or Twice A Month",
  "A Few Times A Year, Such As For High Holidays", "Seldom", "Never"
)

att_plot_df <- att_all_unified %>%
  # drop all other labels
  filter(VariableClean %in% att_levels) %>%
  # clean variable labels
  mutate(
    Variable = factor(str_wrap(VariableClean, width = 20),
                      levels = str_wrap(att_levels, width = 20)),
    Source = factor(Source,
                    levels = c("pew", "unweighted", "raked.sample", "raked.pew",
                               "ipw", "ipw.5", "ipw.8", "ipw.10", "ipw.12",
                               "ipw.raked.sample", "ipw.raked.pew", "ipw.raked.margins")))  %>%
    mutate(Variable = forcats::fct_rev(Variable)) %>%
  mutate(Source = forcats::fct_rev(Source))

legend_order <- rev(c(
  "pew",
  "unweighted",
  "raked.pew",
  "ipw",
  "ipw.5",
  "ipw.8",
  "ipw.10",
  "ipw.12",
  "ipw.raked.pew",
  "ipw.raked.margins"
))

# plot
ggplot(att_plot_df, aes(x = Variable, y = Estimate, color = Source)) +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = CI_lower, ymax = CI_upper),
                width = 0.2, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  xlab("") +
  scale_color_discrete(
    name = "Source",
    labels = c(
      "pew"          = "2020 Pew Survey",
      "unweighted"   = "2025 BISG Survey - Unweighted",
      "raked.sample" = "2025 BISG Survey - Raked to Sample",
      "raked.pew"    = "2025 BISG Survey - Raked to Pew",
      "ipw"          = "2025 BISG Survey - IPW",
      "ipw.5"        = "2025 BISG Survey - IPW (5/95 trim)",
      "ipw.8"        = "2025 BISG Survey - IPW (8/92 trim)",
      "ipw.10"       = "2025 BISG Survey - IPW (10/90 trim)",
      "ipw.12"       = "2025 BISG Survey - IPW (12/88 trim)",
      "ipw.raked.sample" = "2025 BISG Survey - Raked to Sample after IPW",
      "ipw.raked.pew" = "2025 BISG Survey - Raked to Pew after IPW",
      "ipw.raked.margins" = "2025 BISG Survey - Raked to Estimated Margins after IPW"
    )
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.title  = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.title= element_text(size = 13)
  ) +   theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey85", linewidth = 0.5),

            panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),

  ) + geom_vline(

    ),
```

```{r appendix-kosher plot, fig.height=6, fig.width=12}

var_map <- var_map_for(sample_var = "kosher", pew_var = "KOSHER")

kos_raked <- kos_all %>% filter(Source == "unweighted") %>% select(Variable)

  mutate(VariableUnified = coalesce(Var_raked, Variable)) %>%

# clean labels and variable text

# plot

  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = CI_lower, ymax = CI_upper),
                width = 0.2, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  xlab("") +
  scale_color_discrete(
    name = "Source",
    labels = c(
      "pew"          = "2020 Pew Survey",

      "raked.sample" = "2025 BISG Survey - Raked to Sample",

      "ipw"          = "2025 BISG Survey - IPW",
      "ipw.5"        = "2025 BISG Survey - IPW (5/95 trim)",
      "ipw.8"        = "2025 BISG Survey - IPW (8/92 trim)",
      "ipw.10"       = "2025 BISG Survey - IPW (10/90 trim)",
```

## Item ownership

```{r appendix-item-ownership}
# make function to do this for all four

plot_ownob <- function(sample_var, pew_var, title_text) {
# get variables
  var_map <- var_map_for(sample_var = sample_var, pew_var = pew_var)

  # compute results for all designs
  all_res <- imap_dfr(designs, ~ get_results(.x, var_map[[.y]], .y))

# fuzzy match pew to one of the other samples -- select pew and one other
  raked_keys <- all_res %>% filter(Source == "unweighted") %>%
    select(Variable)
  pew_keys   <- all_res %>% filter(Source == "pew") %>%
    select(Variable)
  
# fuzzy match
  matches <- stringdist_inner_join(
    raked_keys, pew_keys, by = "Variable",
    method = "jw", max_dist = 0.3, distance_col = "dist"
  ) %>%
    group_by(Variable.x) %>%
    slice_min(dist, n = 1) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    transmute(Var_raked = Variable.x, Var_pew = Variable.y)

# join pew label onto our label, choose our label
  unified <- all_res %>%
    left_join(matches, by = c("Variable" = "Var_pew")) %>%
    mutate(VariableUnified = coalesce(Var_raked, Variable)) %>%
    select(-Var_raked)

# clean variable text 
  plot_df <- unified %>%
    mutate(
      Variable = str_to_title(
        str_trim(
          str_remove(
            VariableUnified,
            "^(OWNOB_[1-4]|OWNOB_[A-D]|[0-9]+\\s*=\\s*)"
          )
        )
      ),
      Variable = factor(str_wrap(Variable, width = 20)),
      Source = factor(
        Source,
        levels = c("pew", "unweighted", "raked.sample", "raked.pew",
                   "ipw", "ipw.5", "ipw.8", "ipw.10", "ipw.12",
                   "ipw.raked.sample", "ipw.raked.pew", "ipw.raked.margins")
      )
    ) %>% filter(Variable != "99 = Not Answered") %>%
  mutate(Source = forcats::fct_rev(Source))

  # plot
  ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = Variable, y = Estimate, color = Source)) +
    geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = CI_lower, ymax = CI_upper),
                  width = 0.2, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
    xlab("") +
    scale_color_discrete(
      name = "Source",
    labels = c(
      "pew"          = "2020 Pew Survey",
      "unweighted"   = "2025 BISG Survey - Unweighted",
      "raked.sample" = "2025 BISG Survey - Raked to Sample",
      "raked.pew"    = "2025 BISG Survey - Raked to Pew",
      "ipw"          = "2025 BISG Survey - IPW",
      "ipw.5"        = "2025 BISG Survey - IPW (5/95 trim)",
      "ipw.8"        = "2025 BISG Survey - IPW (8/92 trim)",
      "ipw.10"       = "2025 BISG Survey - IPW (10/90 trim)",
      "ipw.12"       = "2025 BISG Survey - IPW (12/88 trim)",
      "ipw.raked.sample" = "2025 BISG Survey - Raked to Sample after IPW",
      "ipw.raked.pew" = "2025 BISG Survey - Raked to Pew after IPW",
      "ipw.raked.margins" = "2025 BISG Survey - Raked to Estimated Margins after IPW"
    )
    ) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.title  = element_text(size = 14),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
      legend.title= element_text(size = 13)
    ) +   theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey85", linewidth = 0.5),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
            panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
    plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5),

    

  ) + geom_vline(
    xintercept = seq(
      1.5,
      1.5,
      by = 1
    ),
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 0.3,
    alpha = 0.6
  ) + coord_flip() + guides(color = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE))
}
```

```{r ces, echo=FALSE}
## make CES survey design
CES25_Common <- read_dta("/data/dataverse_files/CES25_Common.dta")

ces.svy.3 <- svydesign(ids = ~1, data = ces, weights = ~commonweight)

# extract codes from numbers or labels like "1 = MORE THAN ONCE A WEEK"
get_code <- function(x) {
  if (is.numeric(x)) {
    return(as.numeric(x))
  }
  
  suppressWarnings(
    as.numeric(str_extract(as.character(x), "^\\s*[0-9]+"))
  )
}

# recode pew to match, filter to just jewish respondents
pew_plot_design <- subset(pew.svy, get_code(JEWISHCAT) %in% c(1, 2))

pew_plot_design$variables <- pew_plot_design$variables %>%
  mutate(
    attend_clean = case_when(
      get_code(ATTEND1) == 1 ~ "More than once a week",
      get_code(ATTEND1) == 2 ~ "Once a week",
      get_code(ATTEND1) == 3 ~ "Once or twice a month",
      get_code(ATTEND1) == 4 ~ "A few times a year",
      get_code(ATTEND1) == 5 ~ "Seldom",
      get_code(ATTEND1) == 6 ~ "Never",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    branch_clean = case_when(
      is.na(BRANCH) ~ NA_character_,
      as.character(BRANCH) == "REFORM" ~ "Reform",
      as.character(BRANCH) == "CONSERVATIVE" ~ "Conservative",
      as.character(BRANCH) == "ORTHODOX" ~ "Orthodox",
      TRUE ~ "Other / None"
    ),
    race_clean = case_when(
      get_code(RACECMB) == 1 ~ "White",
      get_code(RACECMB) %in% 2:5 ~ "Non-White",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    educ_clean = case_when(
      get_code(EDUC4CAT) == 1 ~ "HS or less",
      get_code(EDUC4CAT) == 2 ~ "Some college / Associate",
      get_code(EDUC4CAT) == 3 ~ "BA",
      get_code(EDUC4CAT) == 4 ~ "Graduate degree",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  # set category order
  mutate(
    attend_clean = factor(
      attend_clean,
      levels = c("More than once a week", "Once a week", "Once or twice a month", "A few times a year", "Seldom", "Never")
    ),
    branch_clean = factor(
      branch_clean,
      levels = c("Reform", "Conservative", "Orthodox", "Other / None")
    ),
    race_clean = factor(
      race_clean,
      levels = c("White", "Non-White")
    ),

    )
  )

    ),

      educ_clean,
      levels = c("HS or less", "Some college / Associate", "BA", "Graduate degree")
    )
  )

# calculate weighted percentages and 95% confidence intervals
# use this same calculation for each variable and survey
# categories have already been combined above, before estimating
get_results <- function(design, variable, panel, source) {
  design$variables$plot_category <- design$variables[[variable]]
  
  estimates <- svymean(~plot_category, design, na.rm = TRUE)
  intervals <- confint(estimates)
  
  tibble(
    Panel = panel,
    Category = levels(design$variables$plot_category),
    Source = source,
    Estimate = as.numeric(coef(estimates)) * 100,
    CI_lower = as.numeric(intervals[, 1]) * 100,
    CI_upper = as.numeric(intervals[, 2]) * 100
  )
}

# attendance estimates
attendance_results <- bind_rows(
  get_results(
    pew_plot_design, "attend_clean", "Attendance", "pew"
  ),
  get_results(
    bisg_pew_design, "attend_clean", "Attendance", "ipw.raked.pew"
  ),
  get_results(
    bisg_margins_design, "attend_clean", "Attendance", "ipw.raked.margins"
  ),
  get_results(
    bisg_ipw_design, "attend_clean", "Attendance", "ipw.10"
  ),
  get_results(
    ces_plot_design, "attend_clean", "Attendance", "ces"
  )
)

# combine results into one file

  attendance_results,
  branch_results,
  race_results,
  education_results
)

# make sure this worked
table(comparison_results$Panel, comparison_results$Source)
comparison_results

# set source and panel order
source_order <- c(
  "pew",
  "ipw.raked.pew",
  "ipw.raked.margins",
  "ipw.10",
  "ces"
)

comparison_results <- comparison_results %>%
  mutate(
    Panel = factor(
      Panel,
      levels = c("Attendance", "Denomination", "Race", "Education")
    ),
    Category = factor(
      Category,
      levels = rev(c(
        "More than once a week",
        "Once a week",
        "Once or twice a month",
        "A few times a year",
        "Seldom",
        "Never",
        "Reform",
        "Conservative",
        "Orthodox",
        "Other / None",
        "White",
        "Non-White",
        "HS or less",
        "Some college / Associate",
        "BA",
        "Graduate degree"
      ))
    ),
    Source = factor(Source, levels = rev(source_order))
  )

# plot percentages and confidence intervals
comparison_plot <- ggplot(
  comparison_results,
  aes(
    x = Estimate,
    y = Category,
    color = Source,
    group = Source
  )
) +
  geom_point(
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
    size = 1.5
  ) +
  geom_errorbarh(
    aes(xmin = CI_lower, xmax = CI_upper),
    height = 0.08,
    linewidth = 0.4,
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~Panel, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, 25)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 100)) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Source",
    values = c(
      "pew" = "#00BFC4",
      "ipw.raked.pew" = "#F8766D",
      "ipw.raked.margins" = "#619CFF",
      "ipw.10" = "#E69F00",
      "ces" = "#7CAE00"
    ),
    breaks = source_order,
    labels = c(
      "pew" = "2020 Pew Survey",
      "ipw.raked.pew" = "2025 BISG: IPW Raked to Pew",
      "ipw.raked.margins" = "2025 BISG: IPW Raked to Estimated Margins",
      "ipw.10" = "2025 BISG: IPW with 10/90 trimming only",
      "ces" = "2025 CES Survey"
    )
  ) +
  labs(x = "Percent", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9, margin = margin(r = 8)),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 10),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "grey85", linewidth = 0.5),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing = grid::unit(1.2, "lines"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 9),
    plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10)
  ) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE))

print(comparison_plot)
```
